proposal.name: Keep the first Python harness failure in receipts

plan.name: Keep the first Python harness failure in receipts
plan.summary: Preserve the first Python collector error through exception chaining, caught errors, poisoning and cleanup, and stop relabeling collector failures as application refusals. Add an optional normalized harness_error diagnostic to Python execution JSON, retain the full diagnostic context, and carry that cause into the affected conformance and actually executed larger-run summaries without relying on the last 20 traceback lines or treating diagnostics as accepted observations. Make What failed identify the affected target, check and invocation for ordinary and larger executions, rendering all application text literally in both explicit-component and legacy receipts. Preserve D-0279's declared-refusal checks, rejection of undeclared application exceptions and failed or incomplete observation streams, diagnostic-only execution fingerprint behavior, and the timeout regressions from #645. Update SPEC.md and the README-linked docs/python.md and docs/gate.md to describe these receipts, cite the existing decisions supporting changed SPEC bullets, and leave the new diagnostic-policy decision for the merger to record because plumbing cannot write decisions/.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationGateFirstHarnessFailure801
tests.says: Real invalid holds keep the first collector cause across long exception chains and caught errors followed by poisoned lifecycle operations; execution and conformance JSON and What failed identify the invocation, with no accepted prefix and full normalized diagnostics.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationGateLargerHarnessFailure801
tests.says: A larger driver actually executes and reports its original invalid-hold cause and invocation in JSON and What failed, while ordinary checked execution survives, declared refusals still reach named-action checking, and genuine undeclared application errors still fail.

tests.name: TestPythonHarnessFailureLiteralReceipt801
tests.says: The first harness diagnostic round-trips through receipt JSON and appears with its target, check and invocation as inert literal text in explicit and legacy Markdown, without exposing the full traceback as the short summary.

usage.summary: Wrote `plan.json` and three acceptance tests covering first-error retention, larger runs, and safe receipts. Check passed: all three tests fail on the base code; the change touches the trusted base and requires a person to merge.
